- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or use moving average to smooth.
- If model forecast is significantly below recent 5-day average, consider mean reversion bias — increase forecast toward historical mean or 10-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns positive after 5–7 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 1.00 → 0.00 → 1.00), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% buffer to forecast for next reversal window.
- Avoid forecasting below 65% of recent 10-day low unless sentiment is strongly bullish — otherwise, model underestimates support levels.
